text:
Alex: Hey all, spotted a sharp p99 step for /v1/generate (model=redwood-large, region=eu-west) starting ~2025-02-23 09:12 UTC. p50/p95 look normal, step lasts ~8m then back to baseline.
Maya: I saw the alert. Any recent routing changes or sampling bumps?
Alex: No manual deploys. Only affects a few endpoints under that model+region.
Sam: p99-only often means aggregation artifacts. Are we merging t-digests from shards with different params?
Elaine: I pulled individual traces around the window — single-request latencies look normal. But the hourly rollup shows a discrete jump at 09:12:15.
InfraBot: [alert] latency-p99-threshold-exceeded /v1/generate (eu-west)
Jun: Paste the rollup query you used? want to check time window and grouping.
Alex: ```sql
SELECT endpoint, quantileTDigest(0.99)(lat_ms)
FROM requests
WHERE timestamp >= '2025-02-23 08:50' AND timestamp < '2025-02-23 09:30'
GROUP BY endpoint;
```
Maya: query seems reasonable. Did any shard change sampling rate or compression params around 09:10-09:12?
Sam: We bumped canary sampling 10%->50% at 09:10 for a subset of customers. That, combined with routing affinity changes, could concentrate taily clients.
Elaine: But the behavior is region-scoped to eu-west. Canaries were global tho.
Jun: We did roll out a routing affinity rule at 09:09 that biases certain orgs to eu-west. If those orgs overlapped with the canary bump, load and sampling could be skewed in that region.
Alex: So two coincident changes: sampling increase + routing preference = skewed merged tdigest. Could look like a p99 degradation in the rollup but not in raw traffic.
Maya: Action list: 1) recompute p99 from raw rows (no tdigest) for the window; 2) check per-shard sampling logs; 3) verify tdigest compression metadata across aggregators.
InfraBot: [deploy] quantile-raw-job started by Sam at 2025-02-23T09:22:10Z
Sam: Raw quantile job finished: p99 for /v1/generate (redwood-large, eu-west) = 160ms (baseline ~165ms). No user-facing regression.
Jun: Root cause: one aggregator was emitting t-digest with compression c=300 while others used c=100 after the canary bump. Merging incompatible compressions distorted high-quantiles.
Alex: Ok — dashboard value reflected the merged artifact. We need guardrails so dashboards don't silently display misleading percentiles.
Maya: UX idea: show a yellow caution icon on percentile panels when shard metadata disagrees, with tooltip: "Percentile merge inconsistent across shards — treat as approximate".
Sam: I'll file an eng-platform RFC for metric integrity checks and panel UX change. Also add a nightly audit that verifies tdigest params across aggregators and alerts on mismatch.
Elaine: I'll add a runbook snippet for oncall: steps to distinguish real latency regressions from aggregation artifacts (raw-quantile job, check sampling logs, inspect shard metadata).
Jun: I'll hotfix aggregators to include compression param in rollup metadata and refuse to merge without normalization.
InfraBot: [note] incident labeled informational — no customer impact.
Alex: Thanks team. Saving this thread for follow-ups and RFC link.
Sam: RFC draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/eng-platform/256-percentile-merge-check
Maya: Opening runbook PR now.
